what_this_is: The Workshop row for tools/read-what-is-on-screen: a short watch of the front window on the person's Mac, read as text, with secrets removed on the Mac; and tool:parse-snapshot, the policy half of the Mac app's accessibility snapshot reader (fields out of a snapshot, redacted).

payload.label: Read what is on my screen
payload.job: Read what the person is doing on their Mac as text from the front window (app, window title, page address and visible words), when they switch apps or windows and every minute, for a short watch, so their AIs keep continuity across the day. Never reads password managers, Keychain, Settings or private browser windows, and removes passwords, keys and card numbers on the Mac before anything leaves it. After a window's first read, later reads carry only the lines that changed. Uses no screenshots.
payload.description: Runs on the person's own Mac for `watch_seconds`. It reads the front window's accessibility text (never a picture) when the front app or its window title changes and again after `tick_seconds` of the same window, and answers one capture per read: when, app, bundle id, window title, page address and `reason` (changed or tick). A window's first capture in the run carries its whole `text`; later captures of it carry only the lines `added` and `removed`. An app listed in the rules' never-read apps, a window whose title holds a never-read word, and a page whose address holds a never-read word are skipped before any text is read. Text matching the rules' secret patterns (private keys, API keys and tokens, card numbers, `password:` values) is replaced with [removed] on the Mac before it is returned. When Accessibility is off the answer is needs_access with the words that say what to turn on. Every list in this behaviour is the tool's rules file, read-data/rules.json. The run needs the accessibility-reading capability granted to this tool.

watch_seconds.description: How long to watch the screen in this run

tick_seconds.description: Read the same window again after this many seconds even when nothing changed

text.description: The window's whole text, on its first capture in this run

added.description: Lines new since this window's previous capture

removed.description: Lines gone since this window's previous capture

verify.requires: macOS with a screen, Accessibility permission granted, and /usr/bin/swift (the tool runs it by absolute path, so no stand-in program can replace it)

provenance.source: A screen-reading continuity app's way of keeping the day's context, built 2026-10-15 from reverse engineering: the front window's accessibility text on a window change and a timer, with secrets removed on the Mac

payload.label: Read fields out of a screen snapshot
payload.job: Turn the accessibility elements of one app's window ({ role, label }) into fields through that app's declarative parser row, with emails, card numbers and tokens removed before anything is returned
payload.description: Give app (its name) and elements ([{ role, label }], as the Mac app's reader takes them). The first parser row whose app_contains matches the app is used, else the generic one; it selects elements by role and label pattern and cuts fields out with regular expressions. Every field is redacted with the redact patterns. Answers rows: [{ field: value }]. Triggers, throttle, parsers and redaction: read-data/snapshot-triggers.json; the governor that decides when to take a snapshot is createGovernor in the same file, used by the Mac app's reader.
